recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中可見數個比周圍細胞大 2–3 倍的非典型大細胞，核圓或不規則、染色質細緻、細胞質深藍且有細小空泡；在正常造血細胞之間出現這種大型淋巴瘤細胞，配合切片中竇內分布才考慮血管內大 B 細胞淋巴瘤。
features: Large atypical cells 2-3 times the size of neighboring cells
Round to irregular/indented nuclei with finely granular chromatin; nucleoli inconspicuous to small
Moderate to abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm with fine vacuoles
Admixed normal hematopoietic elements, including erythroid precursors and a vacuolated histiocyte
Aspirate fat space and red cell background
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows scattered large atypical mononuclear cells, 2-3 times the size of adjacent hematopoietic cells, among residual erythroid and myeloid elements. The atypical cells have round to irregular nuclei with finely granular chromatin and moderate to abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm containing fine vacuoles. A vacuolated histiocyte is also present. The large basophilic vacuolated cells are suggestive of large cell lymphoma involvement; in the context of an intrasinusoidal CD20-positive infiltrate on biopsy, findings are consistent with intravascular large B-cell lymphoma.

ddx.vs: Myeloblasts have finer chromatin, higher N:C ratio, distinct nucleoli and possible Auer rods, and are CD34/CD117/MPO positive rather than CD20 positive.
Burkitt cells are medium-sized and uniform with sharply punched-out cytoplasmic vacuoles, and show a CD10+ MYC-rearranged phenotype.
Plasmablasts have eccentric nuclei with perinuclear hof and are CD138 positive, CD20 negative.
Carcinoma cells occur in cohesive clusters with nuclear molding and are keratin positive, CD45 negative.
